title: ECG-image model identifies concurrent low ejection fraction in archived records
summary: A DenseNet121 model learned to identify echocardiography-referenced ejection fraction below50% from ECG images. It reported ROC areas of0.92 on an internal ECG test set and0.88 at another healthcare centre. The study tests concurrent diagnostic-label discrimination, without establishing early warning or clinical benefit.

source_review.scope: Original primary clinical/computational Methods, reference definitions, model evaluation and Results independently read; no operational laboratory sections

evidence.ai_role: A trained convolutional network maps cropped ECG trace images to a concurrent echocardiographic low-ejection-fraction label.
evidence.tested: Development used119,281 same-day ECG/echo pairs from104,697 people. ECGs were randomly split into107,147 training,2,020 validation and10,114 test records. Another centre supplied roughly24,300 pairs; the internal-test Youden threshold0.18 was carried to that cohort.
evidence.unknown: Random ECG-level splitting does not establish separation of repeated patients. The external denominator is24,323 in text versus24,319 in the table. The internal threshold was selected on test outcomes; the external data are archived, not a prospectively frozen workflow. Standardized device images and same-day selected imaging pairs limit generalization; no screening benefit or diagnosis of future dysfunction is established.
